full_judgment:
3. The appellants contend that the time lost in pursuing their application for review ought to have been excluded in reckoning the period of limitation. 

 4. The Emergency Repulsion of Property Act is a special Act and under section 7A it has prescribed different periods of limitation, namely any person who has not accepted an award may under sub-section (1) bring a suit in a Civil Court if the person instituting a suit was present or represented before the Deputy Commissioner within six weeks from the date of the award in other oases within six weeks of the receipt of the notice under sub-section (1) or within three months from the award, whichever shall later expire. 

 In the present case the suit, filed on 4th September, 1967 against the award dated 17th January, 1967, was clearly beyond the prescribed period of limitation. 

 5. Period of limitation prescribed under Section 7 A of the Emergency Requisition of Property Act,1948 cannot be extended under section 14 or under any other provision of the Limitation Act 1908 which has got no application to the special statute. Again there is no scope for review of an order by which an award is made under sub-section (1) of section 7 A of the Act. It is a settled principle of law that review is not a matter of procedure. It involves a substantive right. Such right, like that of an appeal will not be available unless it is expressly conferred by law. In this regard the respondents have correctly placed reliance on Hussain Baksh V. Settlement Commissioner, Rawalpindi (1969) 21 DLR (SC) 456; PLD 1970 (SC) 1 and Manager, Lever Brothers (Pak) Ltd. V. Lever Brothers (Pakistan) Ltd. Sramik Union 25 DLR 242.
